prompt.context: Our client, GGC Health, operates eight Ambulatory Surgical Centers (ASC) on the east coast. GGC Health has consistently been a profitable organization, but over the past two years, their ASCs' cumulative revenues have been flat at $400 million/year. The CEO of GGC Health is concerned about this and has hired your firm to increase revenues by 15%.
prompt.question: How would you help GGC Health increase revenues by 15% (i.e., $60M)?

clarifying_info.a: ASCs are modern health care facilities focused on providing same-day surgical care, including diagnostic and preventive procedures. They are seen as a more convenient alternative to hospital-based outpatient procedures.

clarifying_info.q: Who decides where surgeries are performed?
clarifying_info.a: Physicians generally dictate where the surgery is performed. They can perform surgeries at hospitals or ASCs.

clarifying_info.q: What is the revenue model for ASCs?
clarifying_info.a: ASC revenue equals the number of procedures performed in the facility multiplied by the expected reimbursement per procedure.
No, pricing increases are not possible.
Focus on revenue growth; dismiss questions about cost.

exhibits.title: Physician Group Membership by City
exhibits.shows: A stacked bar chart showing the percentage breakdown of physician specialties (Orthopedic, Neurology, Gastroenterology) in three target cities: Charlotte, Indianapolis, and Nashville.

exhibits.title: Average Reimbursement Rates Per Patient by Specialty
exhibits.shows: A table listing physician specialties and their reimbursement rate per patient.

framework: Increase revenue at existing 8 ASCs: grow number of patients per doctor, grow number of doctors per facility, optimize procedure mix toward higher-reimbursement specialties, attract higher-reimbursement patient types

Expand by opening new ASCs: analyze target markets (demographics, procedure demand), evaluate partnership opportunities with physician groups/hospitals, assess competition (existing ASCs, hospital strength), consider regulatory/reimbursement environment (fee-for-service vs. value-based care)

questions.prompt: GGC Health has identified three candidate cities for a new ASC: Charlotte (30 doctors), Indianapolis (25 doctors), and Nashville (16 doctors). Given GGC Health can open only one new ASC immediately, which city do you recommend?
questions.guidance: Candidate should request the specialty breakdown (Exhibit 1) and build a 3x3 table of doctors per specialty per city by multiplying total doctors by the specialty percentages. An excellent candidate immediately eliminates Nashville because Indianapolis dominates Nashville in every specialty (Ortho: 10 vs 8, Neuro: 10 vs 4, Gastro: 5 vs 4). The analysis then proceeds to compare Charlotte vs Indianapolis on revenue.

math.setup: Multiply number of doctors per city by specialty mix percentages from Exhibit 1 to get doctors per specialty per city.
steps: Nashville eliminated: Indianapolis has more doctors in every specialty than Nashville
math.answer: Nashville is immediately eliminated. Proceed to compare Charlotte and Indianapolis on revenue (Question 2).

questions.prompt: Using the city doctor breakdowns, calculate and compare the projected annual revenue for Charlotte and Indianapolis. Patients per doctor per month: Orthopedic = 15, Neurology = 10, Gastroenterology = 12.
questions.guidance: Candidate should ask for reimbursement rates (prompt reveal of Exhibit 2), then calculate patients/year per doctor per specialty, multiply by reimbursement rate to get revenue per doctor per year, then multiply by doctors per city per specialty and sum. Indianapolis generates the most revenue at ~$49.8M but falls short of the $60M target alone.

math.setup: Revenue = (patients/doctor/month * 12 months) * reimbursement rate/patient * number of doctors in that specialty in that city.
steps: Indianapolis ($49.8M) > Charlotte ($37.08M) > Nashville ($27.84M); Indianapolis is the preferred city
Gap to $60M target: $60M - $49.8M = $10.2M still needed from other sources
math.answer: Indianapolis is the most attractive expansion city at $49.8M projected revenue, but opening one ASC alone does not meet the $60M target. Additional revenue must come from existing sites.

questions.prompt: Since Indianapolis alone does not meet the $60M revenue target, brainstorm how GGC Health could increase revenues at their current 8 ASC locations.
questions.guidance: Candidate should be structured and organized. Strong answers cover: (1) Increase patients per doctor — make ASC the preferred site by offering doctors more scheduling control, better efficiency, better patient outcomes, profit-sharing incentives for hitting volume targets, prioritize high-volume doctors; (2) Increase doctors per ASC — recruit new physicians and new specialties; (3) Optimize product/procedure mix — prioritize high-reimbursement surgeries, add new high-reimbursement procedure types; (4) Expand patient type — consider which payers are accepted (Medicaid/Medicare) and attract patients with higher reimbursement rates.

questions.prompt: GGC Health believes it can add 2 urology doctors to each of its current 8 ASC sites. Each urology doctor brings in 8 patients per doctor per month. Calculate the additional revenue from adding urology.
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognize the urology reimbursement rate ($8,000) is already in Exhibit 2. Calculate total urologists, total patients per year (round to 1,500), then multiply by rate. Result is $12M, which combined with Indianapolis ($49.8M) exceeds the $60M target.

math.setup: Additional revenue = total urologists * patients per doctor per year * reimbursement rate per patient.
steps: Total patients/year: 16 * (8 patients/month * 12 months) = 16 * 96 = 1,536 → round to 1,500
Combined revenue check: $49.8M (Indianapolis) + $12M (urology) = $61.8M > $60M target — target met
math.answer: Adding urology generates $12M in incremental revenue. Combined with Indianapolis ($49.8M), total new revenue is ~$61.8M, exceeding the $60M target.

brainstorming.prompt: How can GGC Health increase revenues at its current 8 ASC locations?

categories.name: Increase patients per doctor
ideas: Make ASC the preferred site for physicians by offering more control over the environment
Improve scheduling efficiency and patient outcomes to attract physicians
Provide doctors a higher share of profits for hitting volume targets

categories.name: Increase doctors per ASC
ideas: Recruit physicians in new specialties not currently offered
Expand physician outreach through sales and marketing efforts to attract more doctors to each site

categories.name: Optimize procedure/product mix
ideas: Prioritize high-reimbursement surgeries to increase revenue per patient
Add new high-reimbursement surgical procedures (e.g., urology, neurology)
Shift mix away from low-reimbursement procedures where possible

categories.name: Expand patient types and payer mix
ideas: Attract patients with higher-reimbursement insurance plans
Add new procedures that draw different patient demographics

recommendation: Open a new ASC in Indianapolis, projected to generate $49.8M in annual revenue
Add 2 urology doctors to each of the 8 existing ASC sites, generating an additional $12M in annual revenue
Combined, these two initiatives generate approximately $61.8M in new revenue, exceeding the 15% ($60M) target
risks: No cost analysis was performed for adding a new facility or new procedures — profitability is unconfirmed
Indianapolis is not on the east coast and may be unfamiliar territory for GGC Health management
Existing ASC capacity may be insufficient to accommodate new surgeries and additional doctors
GGC Health may not capture the expected market share in a new city
Physicians may not bring in the projected number of patients
next_steps: Conduct a full cost/benefit analysis for the Indianapolis location before committing to construction
If still financially attractive, begin planning and construction on the new Indianapolis ASC
Add urology surgeries to current ASC sites as quickly as possible
Evaluate other new procedure types that could further increase same-site revenue
Assess feasibility of expanding into more than one new city over the medium term
